chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever takes the scales in his hand and intends to take a full measure for himself will only take it with excess; and whoever gives and intends to give an equal measure will only give deficiently.

key_terms.الْمِيزَانَ: the scale or instrument of weighing used in transactions
key_terms.رَاجِحًا: heavier or more than the due amount
key_terms.سَوَاءً: an equal measure, intending exact equivalence
key_terms.نَاقِصًا: deficient, less than what is due

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about fairness when weighing and measuring in trade?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches ethical caution in buying and selling, warning that a person measuring for himself tends toward taking extra, while one aiming merely at equality in giving may end up giving less than due. It encourages fairness, conscientiousness, and moral restraint in commercial dealings.
